title: Standardising "Use By" and "Best Before" Date Labels for Food to Reduce Confusion
what_it_is: Standardising "Use By" and "Best Before" Date Labels for Food to Reduce Confusion

sections.label: Date-mark terms and industry compliance
sections.summary: Both "use by" and "best before" are internationally accepted Codex terms, and standardising to one term would add compliance burden for industry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for
sentences.text: Sustainability and the Environment): Sir, both "use by" and "best before" are internationally accepted terms under the Codex General Standard for the Labelling of Prepackaged Foods (Codex) and commonly used by food manufacturers both locally and overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for
sentences.text: Standardising the use of date-marks to a specific term will require the industry to tailor their packaging to the Singapore market, adding to compliance burden.

sections.label: Expiry dates under food regulations
sections.summary: Under current food regulations, both "use by" and "best before" indicate expiry dates beyond which food cannot be sold in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for
sentences.text: Under the current food regulations, "use by" and "best before" are both used to indicate the expiry date on food products, beyond which, the food product is not permitted to be sold in Singapore due to possible deterioration in food quality.

sections.label: Consumers must treat terms as equivalent
sections.summary: Asking house brands to comply to one standard will not resolve the problem, so consumers must treat both terms as equivalent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, asking our house brands to comply to one standard will not resolve the problem.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It means that at the end of the day, the consumer must take both "use by" and "best before" as equivalent to mean that anything after that date, the food is unlikely to be fresh or may not be in its original state that is fit for consumption.

sections.label: Past dates and proper storage
sections.summary: Food can go bad if not stored properly even when the "use by" date is valid, so consumers should treat any past date as not fit for consumption.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Because even if the "use by" date is still valid and if we do not store the food properly, the food can also go bad.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Regardless of what the "use by" date is, the milk may not be fit for consumption by the next day.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, I think also some common sense is needed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But what I am trying to say here is, whatever the label, as long as the date is past, consumers should treat it as not fit for consumption and think carefully about consuming it.
